subject: Interim findings and corrective roadmap — token coherence mismatch
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Sara Hart <sara.hart@lakebank.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-03-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Observed token-*coherence* mismatches during your 03/29 traffic window — immediate next steps

Sara —

Thanks for the quick alert this morning and for the traces you pasted into the ticket. We’ve started an initial analysis and want to share what we know right away so you have context while we investigate.

Summary (interim):
- We observed a small subset (~0.4% of requests) for LakeBank that returned divergent token sequences (content drift) compared to baseline responses.
- Divergence correlates with requests served by your Dedicated pool during a partial rollout that occurred 03/28 22:40 UTC.

Immediate asks:
1) Can your team preserve the example request ids in the HubSpot ticket (RED-7891) for verification?
2) We will collect epoch logs and KV-cache snapshots for the 03/28 22:30–23:15 UTC window — please confirm retention is OK.

We’ve looped in David and Marissa from Reliability to lead the technical work; Karthik will manage customer verification. Expect an update with a short timeline within 3 business hours.

Apologies for the disruption — we are treating this as high priority.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

Attachments: referenced in follow-up (timeline export, preliminary logs)
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-03-29T11:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observed token-*coherence* mismatches — initial triage

Soojin —

Quick internal notes while I dig into the logs:
- Hypothesis A: A partial deployment of a model variant to a subset of Dedicated nodes created a mismatch between model shard mapping and the KV prefix namespace. The result: some requests used an incompatible KV cache state and produced different continuations.
- Hypothesis B (lower likelihood): A transient orchestration race during rollout produced interleaved tokenization versions for a small batch of sessions.

Planned actions (owners):
- Collect epoch logs, model checksums, and KV-cache digests for affected machines (David) — ETA 2 hours.
- Temporarily disable auto-rollout on the pool that served LakeBank traffic (Marissa) — DONE 10:58 UTC.
- Prepare a customer-friendly RCA and verification plan (Soojin / Karthik) — ETA 6 hours.

I’ll attach checksums and a short script to validate cache/model alignment once we have the artifacts.

-David
David Kim
Principal Reliability Engineer
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Sara Hart <sara.hart@lakebank.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-03-30T14:25:00-07:00
Subject: RCA and corrective roadmap — token coherence mismatch (03/28 22:40 UTC window)

Sara —

Thanks again for your patience. Attached is the formal interim RCA (token-coherence-rca.pdf) and the raw timeline export (timeline-epoch-logs.csv). Below is an executive summary and the concrete action plan we will execute this week.

Executive summary (concise):
- Root cause: During a staged model rollout on 2025-03-28 22:40 UTC, a deployment orchestration edge-case allowed a small fraction of Dedicated worker nodes to run a model binary with a mismatched tokenizer-mapping metadata. That binary accepted the same prefix keys but interpreted them differently, causing KV-cache collisions and divergent token outputs.
- Impact: ~0.4% of requests for LakeBank during 22:30–23:10 UTC experienced content divergence; no customer data was exposed or exfiltrated.
- Why it escaped our guards: Pre-deploy checks validated model file checksums but not the tokenizer-mapping artifact that lives separately in the build pipeline. The rollout system did not compare tokenizer mappings across nodes before traffic cutover.

Timeline (high level):
- 2025-03-28 22:40 UTC — Staged rollout initiated to Dedicated pool A.
- 2025-03-28 22:44 UTC — ~first divergent request observed by LakeBank telemetry (sample id LB-req-2239).
- 2025-03-28 22:50–23:10 UTC — ~0.4% of traffic routed to mixed-version nodes; divergence continues.
- 2025-03-29 09:10 UTC — LakeBank reported anomalies to support; ticket RED-7891 opened.
- 2025-03-29 10:00 UTC — We paused the rollout and began artifact collection.

Corrective actions (short term, owners, ETA):
1) Rollback and resync (David) — Immediately rolled back affected nodes to previous stable binary and reloaded consistent tokenizer mapping. Completed 2025-03-29 10:12 UTC.
2) Verification run (Karthik) — We will run a deterministic verification harness across a preserved sample set from your telemetry and our replay logs; ETA 2025-03-31 EOD.
3) Patch deployment pipeline (Engineering) — Add a validation step that verifies tokenizer-mapping equivalence across all target nodes before traffic cutover. ETA for gated rollout: 2025-04-10.
4) Proactive monitors (Reliability) — New synthetic checks for token drift during rollouts and an alert that triggers a rollback within 30s if divergence exceeds threshold. ETA: 2025-04-03.

Customer-facing deliverables we will share:
- Token-coherence interim RCA PDF (attached).
- Timeline CSV with per-request digests (attached).
- Verification runbook and schedule (verification-runbook.md).

Compensation/credits: We’ll follow the account’s SLA and Marissa will propose a goodwill credit in parallel with your CS team.

Next steps for LakeBank:
- We plan to run the verification harness against your preserved sample set on 03/31 and share the results. Please confirm the sample ids in RED-7891 remain available.
- If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-minute technical walk-through with our eng team.

I’ve included the attachments and the HubSpot ticket link below. I’ll follow up with the verification report once complete.

Apologies again for the interruption — we take this seriously and are implementing changes to prevent recurrence.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

Attachments: token-coherence-rca.pdf, timeline-epoch-logs.csv, verification-runbook.md
From: Sara Hart <sara.hart@lakebank.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-03-30T18:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RCA and corrective roadmap — token coherence mismatch (03/28 22:40 UTC window)

Thanks Soojin — appreciated the thorough summary. A couple quick items: 
- We confirm sample ids in RED-7891 are preserved and we consent to Redwood using them for verification.
- Please include the per-node checksums and the deterministic harness output when you send the verification results.

Also requesting the following as part of the verification packet:
1) A short checklist we can run on our side to confirm that the corrective rollout guard is active in our Dedicated pool after the patch.
2) A timeline for when the deployment-pipeline patch will be staged to pre-prod so we can validate it in our test environment.

We’re available for a 30-minute call 03/31 between 10:00–12:00 PT if you’d like to run through the artifacts live.

— Sara
Sara Hart
Head of ML Platforms, LakeBank

- Included in the Drive folder: per-node checksums, harness output, and a short self-checklist you can run in your Dedicated tenant.

- Marissa will propose the goodwill credit via your CS contact by 2025-04-02.

If everything looks good on your side we will mark the incident as closed and ship the final RCA package to your security team. Please reply to confirm closure.

Thanks for working through this with us — we’ll keep you updated on the pipeline patch progress.

— Soojin
